title: Second Conditional
subtitle: Talk about unreal or unlikely situations in the present and the future.
objectives: Form the second conditional for unreal/unlikely present or future situations
Use "were" for all subjects in "If I were you..."

content.intro: You already know real conditionals (zero and first). Now let's talk about the imaginary: what would happen if things were different now or in the future.

rules.heading: Second conditional — unreal present/future
rules.body:
If + past simple, would + base verb. Used for something imaginary, unlikely, or impossible now.

  • If I won the lottery, I would travel the world. (I probably won't win)
  • If I were you, I would apologize. (I'm not you — imaginary advice)

examples: If I won the lottery, I would travel the world.
If I were you, I would apologize.
If it rained, we would stay home. (unlikely, hypothetical)

commonMistakes.wrong: If I win the lottery, I would travel the world.
commonMistakes.right: If I won the lottery, I would travel the world.
commonMistakes.why: The "if" clause of the second conditional needs the past simple, not the present.

commonMistakes.wrong: If I was you, I would apologize.
commonMistakes.right: If I were you, I would apologize.
commonMistakes.why: In the second conditional, "were" is used for all subjects (including I/he/she) in this fixed expression.

exercises.title: Fill in the Blanks (Part 1 of 3)
exercises.instructions: Complete each sentence with the correct second or third conditional form.

items.prompt: If I ___ (win) the lottery, I ___ (travel) the world.
items.explanation: Unreal/unlikely present — second conditional.

items.prompt: If I ___ (be) you, I ___ (apologize).
items.explanation: "Were" is used for all subjects in this fixed second-conditional expression.

items.prompt: If I ___ (have) more time, I ___ (learn) another language.
items.explanation: Unreal/unlikely present — second conditional.

items.prompt: If I ___ (be) taller, I ___ (play) basketball.
items.explanation: Unreal present — second conditional.

items.prompt: If I ___ (have) wings, I ___ (fly) everywhere.
items.explanation: Unreal present — second conditional.

items.prompt: Which sentence describes an unlikely present/future situation?
options: If I were rich, I would buy a house.
If you heat water, it boils.
If I had studied, I would have passed.
items.explanation: This is the second conditional — unreal present/future.

items.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses "were" for all subjects?
options: If I was you, I'd wait.
If I were you, I'd wait.
If I am you, I'd wait.
items.explanation: "Were" is used for all subjects in this hypothetical.

items.prompt: Which sentence is a second conditional?
options: If I win, I will celebrate.
If I won, I would celebrate.
If I had won, I would have celebrated.
items.explanation: An unreal present/future situation — second conditional.

items.prompt: How do you ask a hypothetical question about the present?
options: What would you do if you won the lottery?
What will you do if you win the lottery?
What did you do if you won the lottery?
items.explanation: A second-conditional question uses would + subject + base verb in the result clause.

items.prompt: Which question is correctly formed?
options: If you were rich, would you travel?
If you were rich, will you travel?
If you are rich, would you travel?
items.explanation: The if-clause stays in the past simple/perfect even in a question; only the result clause inverts with would.

items.prompt: Which sentence describes an unlikely present/future situation?
options: If I were president, I would change the law.
If it rains, I will stay home.
If I had known, I would have told you.
items.explanation: This is the second conditional — unreal present/future.

items.incorrect: If I win the lottery, I would travel the world.
answer: If I won the lottery, I would travel the world.
items.explanation: The second conditional's "if" clause needs the past simple.

items.incorrect: If I was rich, I would travel more.
answer: If I were rich, I would travel more.
items.explanation: "Were" is used for all subjects in this hypothetical.

items.incorrect: If he studies harder, he would pass.
answer: If he studied harder, he would pass.
items.explanation: The second conditional's "if" clause needs the past simple, not the present.

items.incorrect: If we have more time, we would finish it.
answer: If we had more time, we would finish it.
items.explanation: The second conditional's "if" clause needs the past simple, not the present.

items.incorrect: If I were rich, I will travel.
answer: If I were rich, I would travel.
items.explanation: The result clause of this hypothetical needs "would," not "will."

items.incorrect: If she was in charge, she would change things.
answer: If she were in charge, she would change things.
items.explanation: "Were" is used for all subjects in this hypothetical.

items.incorrect: If I had more free time, I will travel more.
answer: If I had more free time, I would travel more.
items.explanation: The result clause of the second conditional needs "would," not "will."

exercises.title: Fill in the Blanks (Part 2 of 3)
exercises.instructions: Complete each sentence with the correct second or third conditional form.

items.prompt: If we ___ (live) closer, we ___ (see) each other more.
items.explanation: Unreal present — second conditional.

items.prompt: If I ___ (not/have) to work, I ___ (travel) more.
items.explanation: Unreal present — second conditional.

items.prompt: If I ___ (have) a car, I ___ (drive) to work.
items.explanation: Unreal present — second conditional.

items.prompt: If she ___ (be) in charge, she ___ (change) the rules.
items.explanation: "Were" is used for all subjects in this fixed second-conditional expression.

items.prompt: If they ___ (invite) me, I ___ (go) to the party.
items.explanation: Unreal present — second conditional.

items.prompt: Which sentence describes an unlikely present situation?
options: If I had more time, I would relax.
If I have more time, I will relax.
If I had had more time, I would have relaxed.
items.explanation: This is the second conditional — an unreal present situation.

items.prompt: Which sentence correctly completes a second conditional?
options: If I were you, I would apologize.
If I was you, I would have apologized.
If I am you, I will apologize.
items.explanation: "Were" is used for all subjects, and the result clause needs "would" + base verb.

items.prompt: Which result-clause form is correct for the second conditional?
options: I would help.
I would have helped.
I help.
items.explanation: The second conditional's result clause needs "would" + base verb, not "would have."

items.prompt: Which sentence uses "were" correctly in a hypothetical?
options: If he were taller, he would play basketball.
If he was taller, he would played basketball.
If he is taller, he would play basketball.
items.explanation: "Were" is used for all subjects in this hypothetical, with "would" + base verb in the result.

items.prompt: Which sentence correctly completes a second conditional?
options: If I had a car, I would drive to work.
If I have a car, I would drive to work.
If I had a car, I would have driven to work.
items.explanation: Second conditional: past simple if-clause + would + base verb.

exercises.title: Fill in the Blanks (Part 3 of 3)
exercises.instructions: Complete each sentence with the correct second or third conditional form.

items.prompt: If we ___ (not/live) so far away, we ___ (visit) more often.
items.explanation: Unreal present — second conditional.

items.prompt: If they ___ (speak) English, they ___ (understand) the movie.
items.explanation: Unreal present — second conditional.

items.prompt: If I ___ (be) an animal, I ___ (be) an eagle.
items.explanation: "Were" is used for all subjects in this fixed second-conditional expression.

items.prompt: If he ___ (have) the money, he ___ (buy) a new car.
items.explanation: Unreal present — second conditional.

items.prompt: If she ___ (not/be) so busy, she ___ (join) us.
items.explanation: Unreal present — second conditional.

summary: Second conditional: If + past simple, would + base verb — unreal present/future.
"Were" (not "was") is standard for all subjects in second-conditional "if I were..." expressions.
